clue.text: Begin to develop large photo

definitions.meaning: a storm or a row that starts up is said to ...

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of the phrasal verb and its noun: a storm or scandal erupting, and a photographic enlargement.

clue.text: Weakness in law that's useful for defence

definitions.meaning: a gap in legislation that lets someone evade its intent
a narrow slit in a castle wall for shooting arrows through

explanation.definitionFit: A loophole is both a legal gap to exploit and an arrow slit in a fortification.

clue.text: Pieces of furniture, not what's outside

indicators.note: what's sits outside the other word, enclosing it

parts.note: what's taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Furniture is described by what it is not.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a paradox about furniture defined by what it isn't; the apostrophe in 'what's' is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A whatnot is a stand with open shelves for ornaments, a piece of furniture.

clue.text: Indicates junction on track not working

parts.note: railway points are the movable rails at a junction
out means out of action, as of a broken machine

explanation.surface: A railway junction is reported to be out of order.
explanation.definitionFit: To point out is to draw attention to, to indicate or show.

clue.text: Show up in port, having rounded one southern cape

indicators.note: the port goes round the other pieces, enclosing them like a ship circling a headland

parts.note: Dover is the Channel port in Kent
the Roman numeral I is one
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: A ship turns up in harbour after sailing round a cape to the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having rounded' sets I, S and C inside DOVER, the Kent port.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something up is to expose or reveal it, which is what finding it out does.

clue.text: Try and cope with dramatic change following its success?

indicators.note: change means alter, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tries to handle a sudden change after a big win.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic and topical: in November 2008 the American party had just won, and its following, its supporters, might be named after its success.
explanation.definitionFit: A political party's following is its body of supporters, which a victory for American democrats would swell.

clue.text: Dry wine giving fellow happiness, endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means without ends, so each word loses its last letter

parts.note: a chap is a fellow, a man
bliss is perfect happiness

explanation.surface: A man is handed endless joy in the form of a glass of white wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the last letters from CHAP and BLISS, giving CHA and BLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Chablis is a dry white Burgundy wine from northern France.

clue.text: Outstandingly — or okay

definitions.meaning: extremely well, to a high standard
an expression of agreement, all right

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both excellently and, as an assent, all right then.

clue.text: Gave revised assessment, it's said

definitions.meaning: marked again, as a teacher regrading work

explanation.definitionFit: Read as re-marked it means graded again; as one word it means commented or said.

clue.text: Old Indian garment found in strange kind of garden

indicators.note: the old garment is placed within the word for strange, so it is found inside it

parts.note: rum is an old British word for odd or strange
a sari is the draped dress worn in India

explanation.surface: A traditional sari turns up in some peculiar garden.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM is British slang for strange; 'kind of garden' is a rose garden, not a general sort of garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosarium is a rose garden, a particular kind of planted garden.

clue.text: Confrontation between packs over a bone

indicators.note: the scrum is laid over the a, covering it so that it sits inside

parts.note: in rugby a scrum is where the two packs of forwards meet head to head

explanation.surface: Two rugby packs clash in a scrum and a bone gets broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' sets SCRUM round A; the packs are rugby forwards, not wolves or cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacrum is the triangular bone at the base of the spine.

clue.text: Representing what's said in pitch one composed

indicators.note: composed means put together anew, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician describes a tune composed in a single pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' signals rearranging PITCH and ONE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Phonetic script records speech sounds, so it represents what is spoken.

clue.text: Fellow not so good, the best one can pick

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS
lower means inferior, of poorer quality

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a man is second-rate, yet he is the pick of the bunch.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on two senses: the flower of anything is its finest part, and a flower is something you pick.
explanation.definitionFit: The flower of a group is its choicest part, and flowers are what people pick in a garden.

clue.text: Body parts, however briefly, shown by lots of people

indicators.note: briefly means shortened, so the word for however is cut to its familiar short form

parts.note: though can mean however, as in 'he did go, though'
races are large groups of people sharing descent

explanation.surface: Some anatomy is on show, though only briefly, in front of a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims THOUGH to THO, the informal short spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoraces is the plural of thorax, the chest section of the body.

clue.text: Superheat, oddly, some running water in Middle East

definitions.text: some running water in Middle East

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange manner, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Water in the Middle East heats up strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like a signal to take alternate letters, but here it rearranges all of SUPERHEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Euphrates is a major river of Turkey, Syria and Iraq, flowing water in the Middle East.

clue.text: River, beginning in trickle, ends in great torrent

parts.words: beginning in trickle, ends in great torrent
parts.note: the first letter of trickle and the last letters of great and torrent are all the letter T, several of which are spelt out as the plural of that letter's name

explanation.surface: A river starts as a trickle and finishes as a mighty torrent.
explanation.walkthrough: The picked letters are not strung together: three copies of one letter make its plural, spelt as the letter's name with an S.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tees is a river of north-east England, reaching the North Sea at Middlesbrough.

clue.text: Element of spoken languages, quite a few

indicators.note: spoken means said aloud, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: tongues are languages; ten is a fair number, quite a few

explanation.surface: An element of speech found in many languages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoken' signals that TONGUES TEN said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tungsten is a chemical element, the metal used in lamp filaments.

clue.text: Service (despite all that) no good

parts.note: even so means nevertheless, despite that

explanation.surface: A church service, for all that, was no good.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening prayer service.

clue.text: Conservative and old-fashioned fool

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative in British politics

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped or made over, so the letters of old are reworked

explanation.surface: A Tory with dated views is dismissed as an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old-fashioned' looks like one adjective, but 'fashioned' is the anagram signal for OLD, making LOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A clod is a dull, stupid person, a fool or oaf.

clue.text: Silly jokes about odd husband's old instrument

indicators.note: about means around, so the jokes surround the other letters

parts.note: corn, short for corny material, means trite humour
rum is old British slang for odd
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Daft jokes are told about a peculiar husband's antique instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: CORN is short for corny humour; 'odd' is the old British slang RUM, not a signal for alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The crumhorn is a curved Renaissance wind instrument with a double reed.

clue.text: Person in position to turn up holding baked dish

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the dish sits inside the verb

parts.note: to occur is to happen or turn up
a pie is a baked dish

explanation.surface: Someone in post shows up carrying a pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' tempts a reversal, but it simply means to happen.
explanation.definitionFit: An occupier is one who holds or lives in a place or post.

clue.text: Second person falling? She barely finishes

parts.note: someone who trips is a tripper, one who stumbles and falls

explanation.surface: Someone trips and goes down, and a woman only just reaches the finish line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely finishes' means ends up bare at the end of her act, not just scraping home.
explanation.definitionFit: A striptease artist ends her performance nearly naked, so she finishes bare.

clue.text: Disorderly tavern's barmaid, for instance

indicators.note: disorderly means in disarray, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the word with its s gives the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A rowdy pub's barmaid is used as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disorderly' rearranges TAVERNS.
explanation.definitionFit: A barmaid is an example of a servant, one employed to serve others.

clue.text: Good way to get into upper-class group

parts.note: an entry is an entrance, a way in

explanation.surface: Someone looks for a good route into high society.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are the class of landed people just below the nobility.

clue.text: Sheet covering Eugene's lover

indicators.note: the word for sheet wraps round the name, covering it on both sides

parts.note: rain that comes down in sheets pours
Eugene Aram was an 18th-century murderer, subject of a Hood poem and a Bulwer-Lytton novel

explanation.surface: A bedsheet is draped over Eugene's mistress.
explanation.walkthrough: Eugene Aram was a real 18th-century murderer; 'Sheet' is the verb for rain teeming down, not bed linen.
explanation.definitionFit: A paramour is an illicit lover, typically a married person's mistress or partner.

clue.text: Poet such as Arnold or Hood

definitions.meaning: Dylan ... and Edward ... were both poets
... Arnold, the Rugby headmaster, and ... Hood, the comic poet, share the first name

explanation.surface: A poet in the tradition of Arnold or Hood.
explanation.definitionFit: A surname of poets such as Dylan, and a forename shared by Thomas Arnold and Thomas Hood.

clue.text: Later adjustment, or net profit after initial losses

indicators.note: each of the three words loses its first letter, its initial

explanation.surface: An accountant revises a figure later, after early losses reduce the profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after initial losses' strips the first letters O, N and P, leaving R, ET and ROFIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A retrofit is a modification fitted after manufacture, a later adaptation.

clue.text: Useless weapon rejected by a politician

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the weapon is read in reverse

parts.note: a gun is a weapon
a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A politician turns down a weapon as useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns GUN into NUG.
explanation.definitionFit: Nugatory means of no value or effect, futile and worthless.

clue.text: Divers from ship's bow getting wet?

indicators.note: a ship's bow is its front, so the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: playfully, becoming wet is becoming un-dry

explanation.surface: Scuba divers drop from the front of a boat and get soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' is the old adjective meaning various, not people who dive.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers, in its old sense, means several or assorted, just as sundry does.
